name: highlighter
title: Highlighter
author: Pluto Systems <https://github.com/plutosystemsco/design-system>
description: Code highlighted in Meridian's roles: tree-sitter with this system's own queries for 21 languages, Shiki for the rest and as the fallback, every colour a code token, for the server or the browser.

files.content:
; Shell, for tree-sitter-bash 0.25.1 (node types read from its
; src/node-types.json at that version). Captures are Pluto code roles.
; written for the Pluto design system; not derived from the grammar's own queries.

; Comments, the shebang among them (the grammar reads `#!` as a comment).
(comment) @comment

; Quoted text of every kind, and a heredoc with its delimiter words.
[(raw_string) (ansi_c_string) (string) (translated_string)] @string
(heredoc_redirect [(heredoc_start) (heredoc_body) (heredoc_end)] @string)

; A command's name is a function: an external program and a builtin alike
; (`curl`, `pip`, `echo`, `cd`, `exit`, `set`), and so is the name a function
; definition gives. A command's arguments and flags stay in the body, the
; owner's ruling, so nothing else in a command is captured.
[(command name: (command_name (word) @function))
 (function_definition name: (word) @function)]

; Builtins the grammar parses as declarations rather than as commands.
(declaration_command ["local" "export" "declare" "typeset" "readonly"] @function)
(unset_command ["unsetenv" "unset"] @function)

; Control words and the test brackets.
["if" "then" "elif" "else" "fi"
 "while" "until" "for" "select" "in" "do" "done"
 "case" "esac" "function"] @keyword
(test_command ["[[" "]]" "[" "]"] @keyword)

; A parameter expansion is meta, whole: `$HOME`, `$1`, `$?`, `${#failed[@]}`.
[(simple_expansion) (expansion)] @meta

; In `${name:-word}`, `${name#prefix}` or `${name:1:2}` an operator after the
; name, and the operand it takes, return to the body; inside a quoted string
; that operand is part of the string. `${#name}`, `${!name}` and `${name^^}`
; stay meta, whole.
(expansion [(variable_name) (subscript)]
  operator: _ @text
  [(word) (regex) (number) (concatenation) (string) (raw_string)
   (simple_expansion) (expansion) (command_substitution)])
(expansion [(word) (regex) (number) (concatenation)] @text)
(string (expansion [(word) (regex) (number) (concatenation)] @string))

; A substitution's body is code again, even inside a string; its delimiters
; are interpolation marks. A delimiter is painted only when the substitution
; is closed, so a half-typed `$(` stays in the body.
(command_substitution) @text
((command_substitution ["$(" ")"] @special) @text
  (#match? @text "\\)$"))
((command_substitution "`" @special) @text
  (#match? @text "^`(.|\\n)*`$"))
(arithmetic_expansion) @text
((arithmetic_expansion ["$((" "))"] @special) @text
  (#match? @text "\\)\\)$"))

; Arithmetic is the one place a shell number reads as a number; `exit 0`, a
; case pattern `0)` and an operand of `[[ $n -eq 0 ]]` are bare words.
(arithmetic_expansion (number) @number)
(binary_expression [left: (number) right: (number)] @number)
(unary_expression (number) @number)
(binary_expression operator: (test_operator) [left: (number) right: (number)] @text)
(test_command (binary_expression [left: (number) right: (number)] @text))
(test_command (binary_expression (binary_expression [left: (number) right: (number)] @text)))

; A regular expression after `=~`, whole.
(binary_expression right: (regex) @special)

; C#, for tree-sitter-c-sharp 0.23.5 (node types read from its
; src/node-types.json at that version). Captures are Pluto code roles.
; written for the Pluto design system; not derived from the grammar's own queries.
;
; No capitalisation rules: C# capitalises methods, properties and classes
; alike, so syntax alone decides. A class used as a static receiver
; (`Console.` in `Console.WriteLine`) is a known loss and reads as text.

; ALL_CAPS names read as constants where they stand as a value or the name
; being assigned. This comes first, so the type, call and attribute patterns
; below take their positions back under last-wins.
((identifier) @constant
  (#match? @constant "^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$"))

; Comments, an XML doc comment's tags included, and a shebang.
[(comment) (shebang_directive)] @comment

; The language's words, contextual ones included where the grammar marks
; them. `true` and `false` are constants, through their literal below.
[
  "abstract" "add" "alias" "and" "annotations" "as" "ascending" "assembly"
  "async" "await" "base" "break" "by" "case" "catch" "checked" "checksum"
  "class" "const" "continue" "default" "delegate" "descending" "disable" "do"
  "else" "enable" "enum" "equals" "event" "explicit" "extern" "field" "file"
  "finally" "fixed" "for" "foreach" "from" "get" "global" "goto" "group"
  "hidden" "if" "implicit" "in" "init" "interface" "internal" "into" "is"
  "join" "let" "lock" "managed" "method" "module" "namespace" "new" "not"
  "notnull" "on" "operator" "or" "orderby" "out" "override" "param" "params"
  "partial" "private" "property" "protected" "public" "readonly" "record"
  "ref" "remove" "required" "restore" "return" "scoped" "sealed" "select"
  "set" "sizeof" "stackalloc" "static" "struct" "switch" "this" "throw" "try"
  "type" "typeof" "typevar" "unchecked" "unmanaged" "unsafe" "using" "var"
  "virtual" "volatile" "warning" "warnings" "when" "where" "while" "with"
  "yield" "__makeref" "__reftype" "__refvalue"
  "Cdecl" "Fastcall" "Stdcall" "Thiscall"
] @keyword

; Preprocessor directives.
[
  "#define" "#elif" "#else" "#endif" "#endregion" "#error" "#if" "#line"
  "#nullable" "#pragma" "#region" "#undef" "#warning"
] @meta
(preproc_arg) @meta

; Literals.
[(integer_literal) (real_literal)] @number
; The literal constants, and enum members at their declaration.
[
  (boolean_literal) @constant
  (null_literal) @constant
  (enum_member_declaration name: (identifier) @constant)
]
[
  (string_literal) (verbatim_string_literal) (raw_string_literal)
  (character_literal) (interpolated_string_expression)
] @string
(escape_sequence) @special

; `$"…{x,8:N0}…"`: the code inside the braces returns to the body; the
; braces, the alignment and the format spec are interpolation marks.
(interpolation) @text
[
  (interpolation_brace)
  (interpolation_alignment_clause)
  (interpolation_format_clause)
] @special
; The alignment's width (`,8`, `,-8`) belongs to the format, not the numbers.
(interpolation_alignment_clause
  [
    (integer_literal) @special
    (prefix_unary_expression (integer_literal) @special)
  ])

; Types. Built-in names, and every name a type field holds.
(predefined_type) @type
[
  (_ type: (identifier) @type)
  (method_declaration returns: (identifier) @type)
  (as_expression right: (identifier) @type)
  (type_argument_list (identifier) @type)
  (generic_name (identifier) @type)
  (base_list (identifier) @type)
  (type_parameter name: (identifier) @type)
  (type_parameter_constraints_clause (identifier) @type)
]

; A qualified name keeps its namespace plain; only the last name is a type
; (`System.Text.StringBuilder`).
(qualified_name name: (identifier) @type)
(qualified_name qualifier: (identifier) @text)
(qualified_name qualifier: (qualified_name name: (identifier) @text))
(alias_qualified_name name: (identifier) @text)
; A namespace in the middle of a member chain (`System.IO.File`) is plain.
(member_access_expression
  expression: (member_access_expression name: (identifier) @text))

; Declared types.
[
  (class_declaration name: (identifier) @type)
  (struct_declaration name: (identifier) @type)
  (interface_declaration name: (identifier) @type)
  (enum_declaration name: (identifier) @type)
  (record_declaration name: (identifier) @type)
  (delegate_declaration name: (identifier) @type)
]

; Methods: declared, and every invocation.
[
  (method_declaration name: (identifier) @function)
  (local_function_statement name: (identifier) @function)
  (constructor_declaration name: (identifier) @function)
  (destructor_declaration name: (identifier) @function)
]
(invocation_expression
  function: [(identifier) @function (generic_name . (identifier) @function)])
(invocation_expression
  function: (member_access_expression
    name: [(identifier) @function (generic_name . (identifier) @function)]))
(invocation_expression
  function: (conditional_access_expression
    (member_binding_expression name: (identifier) @function)))

; `using` and `namespace` names stay plain throughout.
(using_directive (identifier) @text)
(using_directive (qualified_name name: (identifier) @text))
[
  (namespace_declaration name: (identifier) @text)
  (file_scoped_namespace_declaration name: (identifier) @text)
  (namespace_declaration name: (qualified_name name: (identifier) @text))
  (file_scoped_namespace_declaration
    name: (qualified_name name: (identifier) @text))
]

; Attributes: the name is meta, the brackets plain, the arguments code.
(attribute
  name: [
    (identifier) @meta
    (qualified_name name: (identifier) @meta)
    (generic_name . (identifier) @meta)
  ])

; C, for tree-sitter-c 0.24.1 (node types read from its
; src/node-types.json at that version). Captures are Pluto code roles.
; written for the Pluto design system; not derived from the grammar's own queries.

[(comment)] @comment

; Words the language reserves. The type words (`long`, `unsigned`) are left
; to the type rules below, and `NULL` to the constants.
[
  "break" "case" "continue" "default" "do" "else" "for" "goto" "if"
  "return" "switch" "while"
  "struct" "union" "enum" "typedef" "extern" "static" "register" "auto"
  "inline" "__inline" "__inline__" "__forceinline" "thread_local" "__thread"
  "const" "volatile" "restrict" "__restrict__" "_Atomic" "_Noreturn" "noreturn"
  "_Nonnull" "constexpr" "__extension__" "__volatile__"
  "sizeof" "alignof" "_Alignof" "__alignof" "__alignof__" "_alignof"
  "alignas" "_Alignas" "offsetof" "_Generic" "defined"
  "asm" "__asm" "__asm__"
  "__try" "__except" "__finally" "__leave"
  "__based" "__cdecl" "__clrcall" "__fastcall" "__stdcall" "__thiscall"
  "__vectorcall" "__declspec" "__unaligned" "_unaligned"
] @keyword

; The preprocessor: every directive, and a directive the grammar does not
; name (`#pragma`), is meta.
[
  "#include" "#define" "#if" "#ifdef" "#ifndef" "#elif" "#elifdef"
  "#elifndef" "#else" "#endif"
] @meta
(preproc_call directive: (preproc_directive) @meta)

; An include path, in angle brackets or quotes, is a string.
(preproc_include path: [(system_lib_string) (string_literal)] @string)

; A macro's body is raw text to the grammar; when the whole of it is one
; number or one string literal, it takes that literal's role.
(preproc_def
  value: (preproc_arg) @number
  (#match? @number "^[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.']*$"))
(preproc_def
  value: (preproc_arg) @string
  (#match? @string "^(L|u8|u|U)?\"([^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*\"$"))

; Types: built-in, sized, and every name the grammar reads as a type.
[(primitive_type) (sized_type_specifier) (type_identifier)] @type

; Literals.
[(number_literal)] @number
[(string_literal) (char_literal) (concatenated_string)] @string
[(escape_sequence)] @special
[(true) (false) (null)] @constant

; An ALL_CAPS name read or assigned is a constant. Callees, definitions and
; macro names are claimed again below, so their own roles win.
((identifier) @constant
  (#match? @constant "^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$"))

; A function's name where it is declared or defined, through any pointers.
(function_declarator
  declarator: (identifier) @function
  parameters: (parameter_list))

; A call. A function-like macro (`MAX(a, b)`) parses as a call and is one.
(call_expression
  function: [
    (identifier) @function
    (field_expression field: (field_identifier) @function)
    (parenthesized_expression (identifier) @function)
  ])

; The name a `#define` gives, object-like or function-like.
[
  (preproc_def name: (identifier) @meta)
  (preproc_function_def name: (identifier) @meta)
]

; Enumerators are constants wherever they are named.
(enumerator name: (identifier) @constant)

; Attributes: `[[nodiscard]]`, `__attribute__((packed))`. The name is meta,
; its brackets stay in the body.
(attribute_declaration
  (attribute [name: (identifier) prefix: (identifier)] @meta))
(attribute_specifier "__attribute__" @meta)
(attribute_specifier (argument_list (identifier) @meta))

; C++, for tree-sitter-cpp 0.23.4 (node types read from its
; src/node-types.json at that version). Captures are Pluto code roles.
; written for the Pluto design system; not derived from the grammar's own queries.
;
; This file stands alone: it does not load c.scm, so C's rules are stated
; again here in the C++ grammar's terms.

[(comment)] @comment

; Words the language reserves. The type words (`long`, `unsigned`) are left
; to the type rules below, and `NULL` and `nullptr` to the constants.
[
  "break" "case" "continue" "default" "do" "else" "for" "goto" "if"
  "return" "switch" "while" "try" "catch" "throw"
  "co_await" "co_return" "co_yield"
  "struct" "union" "enum" "class" "typedef" "namespace" "using" "template"
  "typename" "concept" "requires" "operator" "friend"
  "extern" "static" "register" "inline" "__inline" "__inline__"
  "__forceinline" "thread_local" "__thread" "mutable" "virtual" "explicit"
  "const" "volatile" "restrict" "__restrict__" "_Atomic" "_Noreturn"
  "noreturn" "_Nonnull" "constexpr" "consteval" "constinit" "noexcept"
  "final" "override" "public" "private" "protected" "__extension__"
  "__volatile__"
  "new" "delete" "sizeof" "alignof" "_Alignof" "__alignof" "__alignof__"
  "_alignof" "alignas" "_Alignas" "offsetof" "_Generic" "decltype"
  "static_assert" "defined"
  "and" "and_eq" "bitand" "bitor" "compl" "not" "not_eq" "or" "or_eq"
  "xor" "xor_eq"
  "asm" "__asm" "__asm__"
  "__try" "__except" "__finally" "__leave"
  "__based" "__cdecl" "__clrcall" "__fastcall" "__stdcall" "__thiscall"
  "__vectorcall" "__declspec" "__unaligned" "_unaligned"
] @keyword

; `auto` as a placeholder type is a storage word; `this` is a keyword.
[(auto) (this)] @keyword

; The preprocessor: every directive, and one the grammar does not name
; (`#pragma`), is meta.
[
  "#include" "#define" "#if" "#ifdef" "#ifndef" "#elif" "#elifdef"
  "#elifndef" "#else" "#endif"
] @meta
(preproc_call directive: (preproc_directive) @meta)

; An include path, in angle brackets or quotes, is a string.
(preproc_include path: [(system_lib_string) (string_literal)] @string)

; A macro's body is raw text to the grammar; when the whole of it is one
; number or one string literal, it takes that literal's role.
(preproc_def
  value: (preproc_arg) @number
  (#match? @number "^[0-9][0-9A-Za-z_.']*$"))
(preproc_def
  value: (preproc_arg) @string
  (#match? @string "^(L|u8|u|U)?\"([^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*\"$"))

; Types: built-in, sized, and every name the grammar reads as a type. A
; namespace qualifier (`std::`) stays in the body; the type at the end of
; the path is a type.
[(primitive_type) (sized_type_specifier) (type_identifier)] @type

; Literals. A user-defined literal is one number with its suffix (`10ms`),
; or one string with its suffix (`"x"s`).
[(number_literal) (user_defined_literal (number_literal))] @number
[
  (string_literal) (raw_string_literal) (char_literal) (concatenated_string)
] @string
(user_defined_literal (string_literal) (literal_suffix) @string)
(user_defined_literal (raw_string_literal) (literal_suffix) @string)
[(escape_sequence)] @special
[(true) (false) (null)] @constant

; An ALL_CAPS name read or assigned is a constant (`x = MAX_LINES`,
; `Config::LIMIT`). Callees, definitions and macro names are claimed again
; below, so their own roles win.
((identifier) @constant
  (#match? @constant "^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$"))

; A function's name where it is declared or defined: free, a member, a
; constructor, a destructor, one defined out of its class (`Box::get`).
(function_declarator
  declarator: [
    (identifier) @function
    (field_identifier) @function
    (destructor_name) @function
    (qualified_identifier name: (identifier) @function)
    (qualified_identifier name: (destructor_name) @function)
    (qualified_identifier
      name: (qualified_identifier name: (identifier) @function))
    (template_function name: (identifier) @function)
  ]
  parameters: (parameter_list))

; An operator's definition (`operator==`): the symbol is the name, and
; `operator` keeps its keyword role from the list above.
(function_declarator declarator: (operator_name) @function)

; A call, through any qualifier, member access or template arguments. A
; function-like macro (`MAX(a, b)`) parses as a call and is one.
(call_expression
  function: [
    (identifier) @function
    (parenthesized_expression (identifier) @function)
    (field_expression field: (field_identifier) @function)
    (field_expression field: (template_method name: (field_identifier) @function))
    (template_function name: (identifier) @function)
    (qualified_identifier name: (identifier) @function)
    (qualified_identifier name: (template_function name: (identifier) @function))
    (qualified_identifier
      name: (qualified_identifier name: (identifier) @function))
    (qualified_identifier
      name: (qualified_identifier
        name: (qualified_identifier name: (identifier) @function)))
    (qualified_identifier
      name: (qualified_identifier
        name: (template_function name: (identifier) @function)))
  ])

; The four casts are words of the language, though the grammar reads them
; as template calls.
(template_function
  name: (identifier) @keyword
  (#any-of? @keyword "static_cast" "dynamic_cast" "const_cast" "reinterpret_cast"))

; A concept names a constraint on types: a type.
(concept_definition name: (identifier) @type)

; The name a `#define` gives, object-like or function-like.
[
  (preproc_def name: (identifier) @meta)
  (preproc_function_def name: (identifier) @meta)
]

; Enumerators are constants where they are named.
(enumerator name: (identifier) @constant)

; Attributes: `[[nodiscard]]`, `[[gnu::unused]]`, `__attribute__((packed))`.
; The name is meta, its brackets stay in the body.
(attribute_declaration
  (attribute [name: (identifier) prefix: (identifier)] @meta))
(attribute_specifier "__attribute__" @meta)
(attribute_specifier (argument_list (identifier) @meta))

; CSS, for tree-sitter-css 0.25.0 (node types read from its
; src/node-types.json at that version). Captures are Pluto code roles.
; written for the Pluto design system; not derived from the grammar's own queries.

[(comment) (js_comment)] @comment

; At-rules and the words of their queries.
[(at_keyword) "@import" "@media" "@keyframes" "@charset" "@namespace"
 "@supports" "@scope"] @keyword
[(keyword_query) (feature_name) (important) "and" "or" "not" "only" "of"] @keyword

; Selectors are types: an element, a class or an id with its `.` or `#`,
; the universal and nesting selectors, and a keyframe's `from` and `to`.
[(tag_name) (class_selector) (id_selector) (universal_selector)
 (nesting_selector)] @type
(keyframe_block [(from) (to)] @type)
(attribute_selector (attribute_name) @meta)

; A pseudo-class or pseudo-element is meta with its colons; a selector it
; takes as an argument keeps its own role, a bare word is the body.
(pseudo_class_selector ":" @meta (class_name) @meta)
(pseudo_element_selector "::" @meta (tag_name) @meta)

; Declarations: the property is a keyword, a value word a constant;
; `!important` is a keyword with the query words above.
(declaration (property_name) @keyword)
(plain_value) @constant
(pseudo_class_selector (arguments (plain_value) @text))

; Numbers with their units, and colour literals, are one number span.
[(integer_value) (float_value) (color_value)] @number
; The grammar reads `0.875rem/1.6` as a number and a value word `rem/1.6`;
; that word is the rest of the number.
(declaration
  [(integer_value) (float_value)] . (plain_value) @number
  (#match? @number "^[A-Za-z%]+/[-+.0-9]"))

[(string_value)] @string
[(escape_sequence)] @special

; Functions, and a function this grammar does not know in `@import`
; (`layer(base)`), which it reads as a word and an error.
(call_expression (function_name) @function)
(import_statement (keyword_query) @function . (ERROR))

; Custom properties, declared or read, are meta.
([(property_name) (plain_value)] @meta (#match? @meta "^--"))

; Go, for tree-sitter-go 0.25.0 (node types read from its
; src/node-types.json at that version). Captures are Pluto code roles.
; written for the Pluto design system; not derived from the grammar's own queries.

(comment) @comment

; Literals. A struct tag is a raw string and stays one; escapes live only
; in the interpreted kind. The language's own values are constants.
[(raw_string_literal) (interpreted_string_literal) (rune_literal)] @string
(interpreted_string_literal (escape_sequence) @special)
[(imaginary_literal) (float_literal) (int_literal)] @number
[(nil) (iota) (true) (false)] @constant

; Keywords: declarations, then control flow, then the type words.
[
  "package" "import" "func" "var" "const" "type" "struct" "interface"
] @keyword
[
  "if" "else" "for" "range" "switch" "case" "default" "select" "break"
  "continue" "return" "goto" "fallthrough" "defer" "go"
] @keyword
["map" "chan"] @keyword

; Types: every name in a type position, a type parameter where it is
; declared, and the type after the package in `time.Duration`. A package,
; as a qualifier or in its clause, is the body.
[
  (type_identifier) @type
  (type_parameter_declaration name: (identifier) @type)
]

; A name in capitals is a constant where it is read or assigned.
((identifier) @constant
  (#match? @constant "^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$"))

; An enumeration: a const block counted with iota. Its first spec holds
; iota (alone or in an expression), and every spec of the block names a
; member, the blank `_` aside. A plain constant (`const budget = 3`) stays
; in the body.
(const_declaration
  (const_spec
    name: (identifier) @constant
    value: (expression_list [(iota) (binary_expression (iota))]))
  (#not-eq? @constant "_"))
(const_declaration
  (const_spec
    value: (expression_list [(iota) (binary_expression (iota))]))
  (const_spec name: (identifier) @constant)
  (#not-eq? @constant "_"))

; Functions and methods where they are declared, in an interface included.
[
  (function_declaration name: (identifier) @function)
  (method_declaration name: (field_identifier) @function)
  (method_elem name: (field_identifier) @function)
]

; Every call is a function, capitalised or not, a built-in included
; (`make`, `len`, `append`). Syntax cannot tell a conversion from a call.
(call_expression
  function: [
    (identifier) @function
    (selector_expression field: (field_identifier) @function)
    (parenthesized_expression (identifier) @function)
  ])

; A conversion to one of the language's own types reads as the type.
(call_expression
  function: (identifier) @type
  (#any-of? @type
    "bool" "byte" "rune" "string" "error" "any" "int" "int8" "int16" "int32"
    "int64" "uint" "uint8" "uint16" "uint32" "uint64" "uintptr" "float32"
    "float64" "complex64" "complex128"))

; HTML, for tree-sitter-html 0.23.2 (node types read from its
; src/node-types.json at that version). Captures are Pluto code roles.
; written for the Pluto design system; not derived from the grammar's own queries.

[(comment)] @comment

; The doctype is one meta span; its `<!` and `>` return to the body.
[(doctype)] @meta
(doctype ["<!" ">"] @text)

; Tags: the name is a keyword, a capitalised name a component (a type).
; The brackets stay in the body, uncaptured.
[(start_tag (tag_name) @keyword)
 (end_tag (tag_name) @keyword)
 (self_closing_tag (tag_name) @keyword)
 (erroneous_end_tag (erroneous_end_tag_name) @keyword)]
((_ (tag_name) @type) (#match? @type "^[A-Z]"))

; Attributes: the name is meta, the value a string with its quotes.
(attribute (attribute_name) @meta)
(attribute [(attribute_value) (quoted_attribute_value)] @string)

; Character references in text.
(entity) @special

; A bare `<`: HTML reads `<` as text unless a letter follows it, and this
; grammar opens a tag there anyway (or, at the end of an element, an ERROR).

  (#any-of? @function
    "parseInt" "parseFloat" "isNaN" "isFinite" "encodeURI"
    "encodeURIComponent" "decodeURI" "decodeURIComponent" "setTimeout"
    "setInterval" "clearTimeout" "clearInterval" "queueMicrotask"
    "structuredClone" "requestAnimationFrame" "cancelAnimationFrame" "fetch"
    "atob" "btoa")
  (#is-not? local))

; Calls: the callee is a function; through a member, its last name is.
(call_expression
  function: [
    (identifier) @function
    (member_expression
      property: [(property_identifier) (private_property_identifier)] @function)
  ])

; A capitalised callee without `new` constructs or converts: a type.
(call_expression
  function: (identifier) @type
  (#match? @type "^[A-Z]"))

; The class in `new X()` or `new ns.X()`.
(new_expression
  constructor: [
    (identifier) @type
    (member_expression property: (property_identifier) @type)
  ])

; ── Definitions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

; A named function, declared, a generator, an expression or an overload.
[
  (function_declaration name: (identifier) @function)
  (generator_function_declaration name: (identifier) @function)
  (function_expression name: (identifier) @function)
  (function_signature name: (identifier) @function)
]

; Methods, getters and setters at their definition, in a class, an object
; or a signature.
(method_definition
  name: [(property_identifier) (private_property_identifier)] @function)
(method_signature name: (property_identifier) @function)
(abstract_method_signature name: (property_identifier) @function)

; A class's `constructor` is a word of the language.
(method_definition
  name: (property_identifier) @keyword
  (#eq? @keyword "constructor"))

; A function bound to a name with `const f = () => …` is a function.
(variable_declarator
  name: (identifier) @function
  value: [(arrow_function) (function_expression)])

; Classes, enums and their members.
[
  (class_declaration name: (type_identifier) @type)
  (abstract_class_declaration name: (type_identifier) @type)
  (class name: (type_identifier) @type)
  (enum_declaration name: (identifier) @type)
]

(enum_body
  [
    (property_identifier) @constant
    (enum_assignment name: (property_identifier) @constant)
  ])


; ── Imports ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

; An imported name is most often a function or a class: capitalised is a
; type, ALL_CAPS a constant, anything else a function. A namespace import
; (`* as path`) is a module, in the body.
; Both the imported name and its `as` alias are matched.
(import_specifier (identifier) @function)
(import_specifier
  (identifier) @type
  (#match? @type "^[A-Z]"))
(import_specifier
  (identifier) @constant
  (#match? @constant "^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$"))
(import_clause (identifier) @type (#match? @type "^[A-Z]"))
(namespace_import (identifier) @text)

; ── Types ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[(type_identifier) (predefined_type)] @type

; Modules stay in the body: a namespace's name (`namespace App.Core`) and the
; qualifier of a type (`React.` of `React.ReactNode`), at any of its first
; three segments.
(internal_module name: (identifier) @text)
(nested_type_identifier module: (identifier) @text)
(nested_identifier
  object: [
    (identifier) @text
    (member_expression object: (identifier) @text)
    (member_expression
      object: (member_expression object: (identifier) @text))
  ])

; `typeof x` in a type names a value's type.
(type_query [(identifier) (member_expression)] @type)

; A type predicate's subject (`x is Frame`) is the parameter, in the body.
(type_predicate name: (identifier) @text)

; ── Decorators ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

; Marker and name are meta; a decorator's arguments are code.
(decorator "@" @meta)
(decorator
  [
    (identifier) @meta
    (member_expression) @meta
    (call_expression
      function: [(identifier) (member_expression)] @meta)
  ])
(decorator (member_expression [(identifier) (property_identifier)] @meta))
(decorator
  (call_expression
    function: (member_expression [(identifier) (property_identifier)] @meta)))

; YAML, for @tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-yaml 0.7.1 (node types read from its
; src/node-types.json at that version). Captures are Pluto code roles.
; written for the Pluto design system; not derived from the grammar's own queries.

(comment) @comment

; Scalars. A plain scalar is a string unless the core schema reads it as a
; number, a boolean or null; a GitHub Actions `${{ }}` stays in the string.
[(double_quote_scalar) (single_quote_scalar) (string_scalar)] @string
[(float_scalar) (integer_scalar) (timestamp_scalar)] @number
[(null_scalar) (boolean_scalar)] @constant
[(double_quote_scalar (escape_sequence) @special)
 (single_quote_scalar (escape_sequence) @special)]

; A block scalar's text is a string; its `|` or `>` header stays in the body.
(block_scalar) @string
(block_scalar ["|" ">"] @text)

; Keys, plain or quoted, are the body: Meridian gives a key a colour in JSON alone.
[(block_mapping_pair key: (flow_node (plain_scalar (_) @text)))
 (flow_pair key: (flow_node (plain_scalar (_) @text)))]
[(block_mapping_pair key: (flow_node [(double_quote_scalar) (single_quote_scalar)] @text))
 (flow_pair key: (flow_node [(double_quote_scalar) (single_quote_scalar)] @text))]

; The merge key `<<` is a keyword.
([(block_mapping_pair key: (flow_node (plain_scalar (string_scalar) @keyword)))
  (flow_pair key: (flow_node (plain_scalar (string_scalar) @keyword)))]
  (#eq? @keyword "<<"))

; Anchors and aliases, with their `&` and `*`; tags and directives annotate.
[(alias) (anchor)] @meta
(flow_node (tag) @meta)
(block_node (tag) @meta)
(document [(yaml_directive) (tag_directive) (reserved_directive)] @meta)
